logs.intro: nexcrate records here what it does. Messages are always in English, which makes them easier to look up online when troubleshooting.

mode.title: How much gets recorded?
mode.intro: Something is always recorded, the level only decides how much. Normal is enough for everyday use. Turn on more for a while when you are tracking down a problem.
mode.label: Log level
mode.descNormal: What happened, plus warnings and errors.
mode.descDetailed: Also the details of every step.
mode.descTrace: Everything nexcrate can record. A lot of lines, meant for troubleshooting only.
mode.question: How long should “{{mode}}” stay on?
mode.fixed: The level is fixed by the environment variable {{variable}} and cannot be changed here. If you want to switch it here, remove the variable and restart nexcrate.

lines.title: Messages
lines.levelHint: Shows the chosen level and everything more important.

clear.title: Clear the log?
clear.text: All lines so far will be deleted. This cannot be undone. If you still need them, download the log first. New messages keep being recorded.

account.title: Account
account.intro: The one account you use nexcrate with.
account.languageHint: Applies on every device you log in on.

password.title: Change password
password.intro: Afterwards all other devices are logged out. This one stays logged in.
password.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
password.done: Password changed. All other devices have been logged out.

sessions.title: Logged-in devices
sessions.intro: Log out everywhere ends the login on all devices, including this one. That helps if you forgot to log out on someone else's device.

about.title: About nexcrate
about.intro: Movies, shows and music in one place, with several versions per title.
about.versionUnknown: The version cannot be read right now.
about.tmdbText: Titles, overviews and posters come from The Movie Database (TMDB).
about.tmdbNotice: This application uses TMDB and the TMDB APIs but is not endorsed, certified, or otherwise approved by TMDB.
about.xemText: When releases count a series or an anime differently from TMDB, the mapping of the numbers comes from TheXEM, a community project.
about.musicText: Artists, albums and tracks come from MusicBrainz, covers from the Cover Art Archive. Files without usable tags are recognized through AcoustID.

outside.title: Address to the outside
outside.address: nexcrate can be reached at this address
outside.addressHint: Such as https://example.com/nexcrate. Other programs build “open in nexcrate” from it. Leave it empty when nexcrate runs only at home under its own address.
outside.noBase: nexcrate runs without a sub path. The environment variable NEXCRATE_URL_BASE sets one, after a restart.
outside.base: nexcrate runs under the sub path {{base}} (NEXCRATE_URL_BASE).

update.title: New version
update.switch: Look at GitHub once a day
update.switchHint: Only the newest release is asked for; nexcrate sends nothing about itself.
update.off: Switched off: nexcrate never asks GitHub.
update.notFound: GitHub has no release yet, or the repository is not public.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.intro: nexcrate sends its events to another program, signed with a secret only you and the program know. Nexview needs none; it reads the event stream itself.
webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.urlHint: http or https. It may carry a token of the receiver; the log names only host and port.
webhooks.secretOnce: You see the secret only now. Enter it at the receiver.
webhooks.signature: Every delivery carries X-Nexcrate-Signature: t=<time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of “<time>.<body>”>.
